fixes.what: Increase .screen--statement min-height or reduce .screen--statement padding-top so the statement text and promises do not get scrolled off-screen before the user finishes reading Screen 2 on desktop
fixes.why: In desktop-1.jpg, 'Reimagined Heritage' sits at the very bottom while the promises are still below the fold, and in desktop-2.jpg the title is already scrolled out of view behind the header, splitting the core brand pitch across two scroll stops.

fixes.what: Add Urdu/Arabic script (ولیمہ / رخصتی) or Gurmukhi/Devanagari accents alongside the Persian script on the South Asian ceremony sections (Haldi & Pheras, Anand Karaj, Reception & Walima) or keep their eyebrows strictly English
fixes.why: Having Persian script on Nikah and Walima works for Persian/Afghan families, but South Asian Hindu and Sikh parents looking at Haldi & Pheras and Anand Karaj only see small English eyebrows ('HINDU CEREMONIES') where other sections have rich calligraphic script.

fixes.what: Add a placeholder attribute to the #f-message textarea (e.g., placeholder="e.g. Persian & Gujarati wedding, Spring 2027, ~250 guests in Napa")
fixes.why: The helper text above the textarea is helpful, but a concrete multi-heritage example inside the box lowers friction for couples and parents unsure how much detail to write on first contact.

fixes.what: Move the 'Partial planning, or one or two events of a multi-day celebration' paragraph (.options__note) into a third grid card or give it a bold subheading
fixes.why: South Asian and Afghan families very frequently book venues with an in-house coordinator and specifically need a culturally fluent planner just for the Nikah, Sofreh, or Sangeet; burying this high-converting service in a muted footnote misses inquiries.
